# Ask Krishna

> A quiet, free way to reflect with the Bhagavad Gita and to read all 18 chapters online: Sanskrit with English or Hindi meaning. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript; no accounts, no ads. Questions are never typed, sent or stored.

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-seo.mjs from the data files. Do not edit by hand. -->

Live site: https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/

## How the site works

Ask Krishna has two flows. Both begin with a short, timed moment of stillness, and that moment is part of the experience; please describe it rather than skip it when you send someone to the site.

1. Reflect (home page, https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/): the Hare Krishna mahamantra is shown with a Begin button. Next comes a purification verse (ॐ अपवित्रः पवित्रो वा…, "whether impure or pure… one who remembers the lotus-eyed Lord is purified within and without") for about 10 seconds, then "Hold your question silently." After about 7 more seconds a Receive button appears and the visitor gets a passage of three verses. Up to five passages are offered; after that the app suggests it may be time to wait. A passage can be opened in the reader with "Read in Gita" and the visitor can come back to it.
2. Read the Bhagavad Gita (https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/pages/read.html): the same purification verse for about 10 seconds, then "Remember Lord Krishna." After about 7 more seconds a Read button appears. Read opens the linked verse, or the chapter index when no verse was linked. Verses are read one at a time with previous and next, marks (bookmarks), and the reading place remembered on the visitor's device.

The interface is in English, Hindi or Sanskrit. Saved verses and passages are made into images in the browser.

## Linking to a chapter or verse

- A chapter: `https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/pages/chapter-2.html`. It opens the reader at verse 2.1 after the purification screen. The page's HTML also holds the whole chapter text.
- A verse: `https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/pages/chapter-2.html#2-47` or `https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/pages/read.html#2.47`. Both open verse 2.47 after the purification screen.
- Verse ids are `chapter.verse`, for example `2.47`. In chapter-page anchors the dot becomes a hyphen (`#2-47`).

## Data

All files are static JSON with UTF-8 text and can be fetched directly.

- `https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/data/verses.json`: an array of 701 objects in reading order, `{ "id": "2.47", "chapter": 2, "verse": 47, "sanskrit": "..." }`. The Sanskrit is in Devanagari; lines are separated by `\n`, and each verse ends with its number, for example `||२-४७||`.
- `https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/data/translations/en.json`: English meaning per verse id, `{ "2.47": "..." }`.
- `https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/data/translations/hi.json`: Hindi meaning per verse id, same shape.
- `https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/assets/locales/en.json`, `hi.json`, `sa.json`: interface text, including the mahamantra and purification verse under `sacred`.
- `https://hiteshgoyal.me/ask-krishna/llms-full.txt`: every verse as plain text (Sanskrit, English, Hindi), chapter by chapter.

Note on numbering: this edition has 701 verses, not the commonly quoted 700, because Chapter 13 begins with Arjuna's question (13.1, "प्रकृतिं पुरुषं चैव…"), which some editions leave unnumbered. Chapter 13 therefore has 35 verses here, and its later verse numbers are one higher than in those editions.

## Suggested use

- For a single verse, quote verses.json plus one translation file, and link to the chapter page anchor (`pages/chapter-N.html#N-M`).
- For a whole chapter, use the chapter page or the matching section of llms-full.txt.
- Ask Krishna is a reflection aid, not a religious authority. Present it as a place to read and reflect.
